# dtcloud_elastic_ip (Resource)

Allocates a public (elastic) IP address and, optionally, points it at a port.

The three verbs map onto Terraform directly: create allocates the address, update associates and
disassociates it, delete releases it. `port_id` is the association and the only argument that
writes it; there is no separate association resource. The API and the SDK call this a floating IP.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Allocate a public address and leave it unattached.
resource "dtcloud_elastic_ip" "spare" {
  floating_network_id = var.external_network_id
}

# Allocate and point it at a machine's port. Moving the address to another port
# is an in-place update: the address itself is never released.
resource "dtcloud_elastic_ip" "web" {
  floating_network_id = var.external_network_id
  port_id             = dtcloud_vm_network_interface.web.port_id
}
```

-> **Finding the external network.** `floating_network_id` is the external network, not the network
your machine is on. `GET /openstack/routers/externals` reports, for each of your networks, the
external network it is routed to; `dtctl router externals` prints the same thing.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `floating_network_id` (String) ID of the external network to allocate the address from. `GET /openstack/routers/externals` reports which external network each of your networks is routed to. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `fixed_ip_address` (String) Which address on the port to map to, for a port that has several. The platform picks one when omitted.
- `port_id` (String) ID of the port to point the address at. Remove it to disassociate. A VM's ports are on its `network_interface` blocks: `dtcloud_vm.web.network_interface[0].port_id`.
- `subnet_id` (String) ID of a specific subnet of the external network to take the address from. Only used when allocating, and never reported back — see the note on import. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the address was allocated, in RFC 3339 format.
- `description` (String) Description of the address. Read-only: neither the create nor the update route accepts one, so this is only ever set for an address created outside Terraform.
- `device_id` (String) ID of the resource behind the port — the virtual machine or load balancer this address currently reaches. Empty when the address is not associated.
- `device_owner` (String) What kind of thing is behind the port, as the platform labels it, e.g. `compute:nova` for a VM. Empty when the address is not associated.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `ip_address` (String) The public address that was allocated. This is the value to hand out.
- `router_id` (String) ID of the router carrying the traffic, filled in once the address is associated.
- `status` (String) `ACTIVE` when the address is associated, `DOWN` when it is not. `DOWN` is a resting state, not a fault.
- `updated_at` (String) When the address was last changed, in RFC 3339 format.

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `update` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Moving the address is an update, not a replacement.** Changing `port_id` points the same address
  somewhere else, so an address that is already in DNS or in a firewall rule is never given up. Only
  `floating_network_id` and `subnet_id` force a new address.
* **Disassociation is all-or-nothing.** The update endpoint has no partial mode: a request that names
  no port detaches the address. That is also why the association lives on this resource: two
  resources writing the same field through the same call would undo each other.
* **`DOWN` is a resting state.** An allocated address with nothing attached reports `DOWN`. It still
  occupies quota and is still billed; `dtcloud_elastic_ips` with `status = "DOWN"` finds these.
* **`fixed_ip_address` needs `port_id`.** Setting it without a port is refused at plan time. Left
  out, it is never sent and the platform picks an address on the port, which is what lets the
  address move to a port that does not have the previous address.
* **A port with several IPv4 addresses needs `fixed_ip_address`.** The platform will not choose one
  for you, and what addresses a port has is only known when the call is made, so this fails at
  apply rather than at plan.
* **Changing `port_id` refreshes what the address reaches.** `status`, `device_id`, `device_owner`
  and `router_id` show as known after apply.

## Timeouts

`create`, `update` and `delete` each default to 10 minutes. Allocating and associating are
asynchronous: the provider waits until the address reports the port it was asked for. Override
them with a `timeouts` block:

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_elastic_ip" "web" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    update = "20m"
  }
}
```

## Import

```shell
terraform import dtcloud_elastic_ip.web 5c1e7b93-2fd4-4a08-9b6e-1c3a7d2f8e44
```

`port_id`, `fixed_ip_address` and the read-only attributes are read back. `subnet_id` is not: the
API never reports it, so an imported address has it empty. An empty value is not treated as a
change, so no new address is proposed, but write it into the configuration if it matters which
subnet the address came from.
